title: Reject partial successor payloads on noncommitted historical settlements
evidence: model.rs:237-256 defines successor_shape as transition.is_some() && history.is_some() && candidate.is_some(), then accepts committed == successor_shape. For a noncommit with exactly one or two Some fields, both sides are false.

Take otherwise valid source/selected-transition/target authority, a Rejected outcome, successor_candidate=Some(valid candidate), and the other two successor options None. Source predicates remain true and committed_shape_is_exact is skipped, so local validity succeeds.

Both family encode/decode rely on that predicate; status validates common source authority and skips its successor branch for noncommit, returning a noncommit proof whose successor_candidate accessor can expose the embedded candidate.

Normal current mutation constructors emit either all three successors or none. This is a demonstrated local malformed-record acceptance path, not a claim that ordinary commands currently construct the partial shape or that an exploit was executed.
proposal: Require exactly all three successor fields for Committed and exactly none for every noncommit. A private closed committed payload may express that invariant, provided decoding rejects partial legacy option combinations before construction and persisted bytes remain unchanged.
required_contract_changes: None. The existing V7 schema explicitly disallows a no-change historical adoption naming a successor. This repairs that current contract.
